finding: I overwrote the full JUnit result set with two filtered test runs
whatHappened: In round 177 I ran gradlew test --tests *GateCapTest --tests *WallDecayTest, then gradlew test --tests *WallDecayTest, to verify two assertion guards I had just added. Gradle's test task clears and rewrites build/test-results/test, so 103 XML files covering 629 tests were replaced by a single file covering 2.
howItSurfaced: Round 180's skipped-count check read the directory and found 1 file and 2 tests where 103 and 629 had been. The check was looking for something else entirely.

wasItRecoverable.archivedCopiesSearched: docs/evidence holds 1531 TEST-local*.xml files across 25 directories
wasItRecoverable.verdict: No archive holds the 103-file set, so those specific files are gone.

actualImpact.theCountIsUnaffected: 629 comes from counting declarations in src/test - 611 @Test methods plus 4 @ParameterizedTest expanding to 18 - not from the XML. The number is unchanged.
actualImpact.theRound163VerificationIsStillTraceable: The nine classes added this session, their test counts and their zero failures are recorded in commit f1514c2's message, so the conclusion stands even though it can no longer be re-derived from XML.
actualImpact.nothingElseDependedOnIt: build/run/gameTest and build/reports/gametest are separate paths and were untouched, so the GameTest evidence and the running stress profile are unaffected.
actualImpact.theRealLoss: The ability to re-verify round 163's per-class numbers from the artifacts. They now rest on the commit record alone.

whatIWillNotClaim: No evidence was damaged for the goal's six items. Item 6 asks for compilation of the source sets, and compileTestJava and compileGametestJava both still pass. This affects the audit trail for the unit tests, not the goal's evidence.
theLesson: Running a Gradle test task for a two-class spot check rewrites the shared results directory. A filtered run and a full run write to the same place, so a spot check silently destroys a full run's output.
